output.title: Plan
output.rationale: Keys are a prerequisite for both SQL queries and normalisation, so they come first; activities are recommendations only, not official course requirements.

days.objective: Explain tables, primary keys, and foreign keys to ground later topics
activities: Recommended practice: sketch two related tables and mark primary and foreign keys
Recommended review: recap key definitions in your own words

days.objective: Write basic SELECT queries and join two tables correctly
activities: Recommended practice: write SELECT queries with filters, then a JOIN across two tables
Recommended review: re-run earlier queries and note what each clause changes

days.objective: Understand normalisation steps and why they reduce redundancy
activities: Recommended practice: take an unnormalised table and split it step by step
Recommended review: summarise each normalisation stage in one sentence

days.objective: Connect query practice with normalised table design
activities: Recommended practice: write JOIN queries against your normalised tables
Recommended review: self-quiz on keys, JOINs, and normalisation stages

next_steps: Review progress after Day 4 and adjust pacing

questions.prompt: Table A has 5 rows; Table B has matching join keys for only 3 of them. How many rows does A LEFT JOIN B return?
questions.explanation: A LEFT JOIN keeps all rows from the left table; the 2 unmatched rows have NULL in right-side columns.

questions.prompt: Students has 3 rows; Grades matches only 2 students. Compare row counts and NULL behaviour for INNER JOIN versus Students LEFT JOIN Grades.
questions.ideal_answer: Marking guide: INNER JOIN returns 2 rows (matches only). LEFT JOIN returns 3 rows; the unmatched student has NULL in grade columns. Award marks for both counts and the NULL detail.
questions.skill: Distinguishing INNER and LEFT JOIN behaviour

output.feedback: The response correctly explains both that INNER JOIN returns only rows with matching keys in both tables and that LEFT JOIN keeps all left-table rows with NULLs for unmatched right-side values.
strengths: Accurately defines INNER JOIN matching behavior
Correctly describes LEFT JOIN NULL handling for unmatched rows
improvements: Could add a brief concrete example with two small tables to illustrate the difference
output.next_step: Practice writing INNER and LEFT JOIN queries on sample tables to see the row differences in actual results.

note: Synthetic cases; semantic judgments require human review.
